title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Cross-Tenant Orchestrated Migration

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the guidance incorrectly puts rebuilding security groups after migration and says source tenants cannot run migration commands, although the documented standalone OneDrive and SharePoint moves start there. The batch command combines separate commands incorrectly, and the shared-data licensing statement omits Enterprise Agreement eligibility.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Governance controls
claims.claim: Cross Tenant User Data Migration is a required per-user add-on.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant migrations require a per-user license (one-time fee) and can be assigned on either the source or target user object. This license enables the migration of all content supported by orchestration. Cross Tenant User Data Migration is available as an add-on

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The user migration licence has a one-time fee.
claims.quote: Cross-Tenant migrations require a per-user license (one-time fee)

claims.claim: The migration licence can be assigned to either the source or target user.
claims.quote: can be assigned on either the source or target user object.

claims.claim: Migrations fail without the required migration licence.
claims.quote: If you don't have the proper license assigned to the user being migrated, the migration fails
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-mailbox-migration?view=o365-worldwide#licensing to sources for the licence-failure statement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Shared data migration licences are offered per 100 GB, without an eligibility qualification.
claims.quote: The Cross-Tenant Shared Data Migration feature and licenses are currently only available to Enterprise Agreement customers. ... Licenses are offered on a per 100 GB of data moved basis.
claims.fix: Qualify the notes and cost section: 'For the existing cross-tenant SharePoint migration tool, Cross-Tenant Shared Data Migration licences are currently available only to Enterprise Agreement customers and are offered per 100 GB moved.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-sharepoint-migration and distinguish this from final licensing for the roadmap experience.

claims.claim: Pricing for the roadmap's orchestrated service has not yet been published.
claims.quote: Searched: Cross Tenant Orchestrated Migration pricing price Shared Data Migration 100 GB User Data Migration. Opened orchestrator overview, cross-tenant OneDrive and SharePoint overviews, and the SharePoint licensing link; found licensing terms but no service price.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The documented Migration Orchestrator automatically sequences supported workloads.
claims.quote: The Migration Orchestrator handles sequencing automatically for supported workloads.

claims.claim: Individual cross-tenant tools exist for mailbox, OneDrive and SharePoint migration.
claims.quote: Individual workload migration | Migrating a single workload, or when you need granular control over each workload's timeline | Cross-tenant tools (mailbox, OneDrive, SharePoint)

claims.claim: Mergers, divestitures and tenant consolidations are migration scenarios.
claims.quote: Merger or acquisition ... Divestiture or spin-off ... Consolidation: Your organization has multiple tenants from past acquisitions and wants to consolidate into one.

claims.claim: Learn says migrations are not subject to SLAs.
claims.quote: Migrations are not subject to SLAs.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Identity mapping is required.
claims.quote: Identity Mapping is required, which means the specific user configuration supported by Identity Mapping is required.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant migration requires trust between the participating tenants.
claims.quote: After you connect to the source and target tenant, the next step in performing a cross-tenant SharePoint migration is establishing trust between the tenants.

claims.claim: Security groups need to be recreated or prepared in the target tenant.
claims.quote: Precreate users and groups as needed in the target tenant's directory. ... Precreated users must be added as members of any appropriate security groups or unified groups before the OneDrive migration begins.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-onedrive-migration-step4 and state that target groups and membership must be prepared before migration.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Cross-tenant moves generally are one-way moves with redirects left behind.
claims.quote: Move mailboxes back to the original source ... If a mailbox is required to move back to the original source tenant, the same set of steps and scripts must be run in both new source and new target tenants, with some variance.
claims.fix: Limit the one-and-done, redirect statement to the documented OneDrive and SharePoint moves, citing their migration overviews. Remove the blanket one-way assertion from the risk rationale; mailbox documentation describes a reverse migration, and the orchestrator overview says original Teams content remains in the source.

claims.claim: OneDrive cross-tenant migration does not support incremental or delta passes.
claims.quote: Incremental and delta migration passes cannot be performed.

claims.claim: SharePoint cross-tenant migration does not support incremental or delta passes.
claims.quote: Incremental and delta migration passes can't be performed.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant OneDrive migration is not supported in government clouds.
claims.quote: This feature isn't supported for users of the Government Cloud, including GCC, Consumer, GCC High, or DoD.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-onedrive-migration for this cloud restriction; retain its explicit scope to the existing OneDrive migration feature.

claims.claim: Administrators in both source and target tenants must participate.
claims.quote: To establish trust, each SharePoint tenant administrator must run specific commands on both source and target tenants.

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for creating, validating and running an orchestrator batch.
claims.quote: Searched: cross tenant migration orchestrator admin center user interface create validate run migration batch. Opened Running the migration and orchestrator overview; documented execution uses Graph PowerShell or Graph Explorer, not an admin-center batch path.

claims.claim: The printed Connect-MgGraph; Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob / Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob expression is the call for creating, validating and running a batch.
claims.quote: Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id> ... Once the batch status is ValidatePassed, call migrate ... Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <batch display name or job id>
claims.fix: Remove the slash-combined expression. Show Test-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <id> and Move-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob -CrossTenantMigrationJobId <id> as separate commands, with a requirement to wait for ValidatePassed before running Move. Retain the documented Connect-MgGraph scope. Rename the row to validating and running an existing batch, or separately document creation with New-MgBetaCrossTenantMigrationJob and the required settings from the cited page.

claims.claim: Orchestrator migration commands run in the target tenant as Microsoft 365 Migration Administrator or Global Administrator.
claims.quote: All commands below are run through Microsoft Graph from the target tenant by Microsoft M365 Migration Administrators or Global Administrators.

claims.claim: An orchestrator batch holds at most 100 users.
claims.quote: The maximum batch size is 100 users.

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for SharePoint and OneDrive cross-tenant migration trust.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive cross tenant trust migration admin center UI Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove. Opened both trust step-2 pages; both give PowerShell, not a UI trust path.

claims.claim: Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Target -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <url> requests migration trust with the target tenant.
claims.quote: On the source tenant, run this command to send a trust request to the target tenant: Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Target -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <TARGETCrossTenantHostUrl>
claims.fix: Add a note that this command runs on the source tenant and is only one half of the trust setup. The target administrator must also run Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship -Scenario MnA -PartnerRole Source -PartnerCrossTenantHostUrl <SOURCECrossTenantHostUrl>, as the cited page states.

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for the existing cross-tenant OneDrive move.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive cross tenant trust migration admin center UI Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove. Opened OneDrive overview and step 6; the move is documented through PowerShell only.

claims.claim: Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove with source UPN, target UPN and target cross-tenant host URL starts one user's OneDrive move.
claims.quote: Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove -SourceUserPrincipalName <...> -TargetUserPrincipalName <...> -TargetCrossTenantHostUrl <...>

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for the existing SharePoint cross-tenant site move.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint OneDrive cross tenant trust migration admin center UI Set-SPOCrossTenantRelationship Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove. Opened SharePoint overview and step 6; found a PowerShell move, not an admin UI path.

claims.claim: Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove is the documented cmdlet for moving a SharePoint site.
claims.quote: Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove -SourceSiteUrl <...> -TargetSiteUrl <...> -TargetCrossTenantHostUrl <...>
claims.fix: Replace the bare cmdlet name with the useful documented call: Start-SPOCrossTenantSiteContentMove -SourceSiteUrl <source-site-url> -TargetSiteUrl <target-site-url> -TargetCrossTenantHostUrl <target-host-url>. Note that it runs on the source tenant.

claims.where: controls[4].ui, controls[4].api, controls[4].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: No control for an orchestrated migration admin-center page is documented; current Learn instructions instead describe Graph execution.
claims.quote: Searched: migration orchestrator admin center migration UI; cross tenant migration orchestrator admin center user interface create validate run migration batch. Opened overview and Running the migration; found Graph execution but no admin-center page control or API to configure such a page.

claims.claim: Learn documents orchestrator execution through Graph APIs using PowerShell or Graph Explorer.
claims.quote: Migrations are managed through Graph APIs. These APIs can be run with PowerShell 5 or 7, or with Graph Explorer.

claims.claim: The workload-specific SharePoint and OneDrive commands use SharePoint Online Management Shell.
claims.quote: Microsoft SharePoint Online Powershell. Confirm you have the most recent version installed. Download SharePoint Online Management Shell from the official Microsoft Download Center.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-onedrive-migration and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-sharepoint-migration to sources for the workload tooling prerequisites.

claims.claim: Source tenants cannot run migration commands, stated without limiting this to orchestrator commands.
claims.quote: To start the migration, a SharePoint Admin or Microsoft 365 Global Admin of the source tenant must run the following command: Start-SPOCrossTenantUserContentMove
claims.fix: Replace with: 'Orchestrator Graph migration commands run only from the target tenant. The standalone OneDrive and SharePoint move commands in this table run from the source tenant as a SharePoint Admin or Microsoft 365 Global Admin.' The respective step-6 pages document this distinction.

claims.claim: Validation results expire after seven days.
claims.quote: Validation must pass within the last seven days. If more than seven days elapsed since validation passed, you must revalidate before migrating.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Compliance holds affect migration eligibility and require planning.
claims.quote: Mailboxes on any type of hold aren't migrated, and a move for those mailboxes is blocked. Talk to our engineering team before attempting to move any users with holds applied.

claims.claim: Rebuilding security groups belongs after the migration rollout.
claims.quote: Precreate users and groups as needed in the target tenant's directory. ... Precreated users must be added as members of any appropriate security groups or unified groups before the OneDrive migration begins.
claims.fix: Move security-group preparation to Before rollout: 'Precreate target security groups, populate required memberships and include them in identity mapping before migrating content.' After rollout, verify memberships and permissions instead of first rebuilding the groups.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits an optional admin-opt-in migration capability.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; defaultState: "admin-opt-in". The assessment scale assigns review when nothing changes until an administrator chooses an optional capability.
claims.fix: Set action to review. The verified migration process requires explicit administrative configuration and submission; the sources do not describe an automatic migration or a mandatory deadline.

claims.claim: The controls table covers the operational controls the governance checklist asks administrators to plan or check.
claims.quote: The checklist says 'Plan identity mapping, licences in the target tenant and holds' and 'Rebuild security groups'; the table contains batch execution, trust, workload moves and an admin-page gap, but no rows for these controls.
claims.fix: Add rows for migration identity mapping, licence assignment and hold checks, and target group preparation, within the eight-row limit by combining directly related preparation controls. Research and cite each documented surface rather than assuming a null. Correct group preparation timing as separately noted.

claims.claim: Some associated objects must be rebuilt rather than being moved intact.
claims.quote: Workflows (2010 or 2013) must be re-created and republished on the Target tenant. ... PowerApps and Automation Tasks must be recreated and reconnected to the Site on the target tenant.
claims.fix: Make the vague 'some objects' specific to the existing SharePoint tool: workflows and Power Apps/automation tasks require recreation. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/migration/cross-tenant-sharepoint-migration.
